title: Training program for UTMB: interview with David Roche (Andrew Skurka)
population: Coach guidance for athletes recovering from a 100-mile race
findings: A full-throttle 100 'takes around a full month to recover from for most athletes': a week of rest, a week of slow running, a week of slow running plus a couple of short hills, a week of easy running.
Full fitness and recovery around 2 months.
Returning too soon can manifest similarly to overtraining syndrome.
It is especially risky for athletes doing their first 100.
limitations: One coach's convention from an interview; no data cited; no per-distance figures for 50 km or 100 km. The page's illness details (cough, mononucleosis-like symptoms) were not re-confirmed and were dropped.
implications: A four-week staged return after a 100-mile race (rest, slow, slow with short hills, easy) is a comparator for the engine's 100-mile ramp, and about 2 months to full fitness.
Supports a more conservative return for first-time 100-milers; first-timer status is a plausible input if the engine has race-history data.
